q: 1. The bricks should be burnt at temperature from ............
explain: Bricks must be burnt between 1000°C and 1200°C to achieve vitrification. Below 1000°C, they remain soft; above 1200°C, they may melt and distort.

q: 2. The type of brick suitable for panel walls for multi-storeyed buildings is ............
explain: Both hollow and perforated bricks are used in high-rise panel walls to reduce the dead weight of the structure and provide better thermal insulation.

q: 3. The length of a curved tile varies from ............
explain: Curved or pan tiles used for roofing generally have a standard length ranging from 15 cm to 20 cm as per sunil Sah Book and Geek Mcq But as per google option d .

q: 4. A bull nose brick is not used for ............
explain: Bull nose bricks have rounded corners and are used for aesthetics and safety on pillars or wall ends, but they are not used for structural arches.

q: 5. Second class bricks ............
options: produce a metallic sound when struck
explain: Second class bricks are reasonably well-burnt and should still produce a clear metallic ringing sound when struck together.

q: 6. Jhumb bricks are ............
explain: Jhumb bricks (or Jhama bricks) are over-burnt bricks. They are often vitrified, dark in colour, and used in foundation concrete.

q: 7. The portion of the brick cut across its width and having its length equal to that of a full brick, is known as ............
explain: A queen closer is a brick piece cut longitudinally into two equal halves. It has the same length as a full brick but half the width.

q: 8. The dolomite bricks are ............
explain: Dolomite bricks are refractory bricks used in furnace linings. Chemically, they are basic because they contain calcium and magnesium oxides.

q: 9. King closers are related to ............
explain: A king closer is a type of brick cut used in masonry where one corner is cut off so the width at one end is half the full width.

q: 10. Generally wooden moulds are made from ............
explain: Sisham is often preferred over teak because it is generally more affordable while providing excellent longevity and stability, according to IndiaBIX and ZoneTech.

q: 11. The kiln which may work throughout the year, is ............
explain: Hoffman's kiln is a continuous, permanent structure with a roof, allowing brick burning to continue even during the rainy season.

q: 12. Excess of silica in the clay ............
options: makers the brick brittle and weak
makes the brick crack and warp on drying
changes colour of the brick from red to yellow
improves impermeability and durability of the brick
explain: Silica prevents shrinkage, but if present in excess, it destroys the cohesion between clay particles, making the brick brittle.

q: 13. Which of the following constituent, when present in excess quantity in clay causes the bricks to melt and distort during burning?
explain: Excess lime acts as a flux during burning, causing the bricks to fuse, melt, and lose their shape.

q: 14. The alkaline salt present in the bricks, absorbs moisture from the air which on drying ............
options: leaves pores and makes the bricks porous
leaves high powder deposit on the brick
makes the bricks brittle and weak
explain: Alkalies cause 'efflorescence', where white powdery salt deposits appear on the surface of the brick after moisture evaporates.

q: 15. The good clay for making bricks is ............
explain: Weathering (exposure to atmosphere for several months) improves the plasticity and uniformity of the clay for brick making.

q: 16. The process of mixing clay, water and other ingredients to make bricks, is known as ............
explain: As Per Book Key And Zone tech ,The process of mixing clay, water and other ingredients to make bricks is known as kneading.Tempering means converting of the prepared brick earth into a homogeneous mix of the desired plasticity by mixing it thoroughly with proper quantities of water.The process of working and tempering clay to make it plastic and of uniform consistency is known as pugging.

q: 17. The bricks after moulding should be dried in ............
options: air for 3 to 8 days but not in sun
explain: Bricks should be dried in the shade (protected from direct sun) to prevent uneven drying and cracking.

q: 18. The indentation marks left on bricks during the process of moulding, are known as ............
explain: The 'frog' is the depression on the top face of the brick. It serves as a key for mortar and often displays the manufacturer's name.

q: 19. The average out-turn of first class bricks in clamp burning is about ............
explain: Clamps are less efficient than kilns; typically only about 60% of bricks from a clamp are first-class quality.

q: 20. The average out-turn of first class bricks in kiln burning is ............
explain: Kilns offer better control over temperature, yielding a higher first-class brick out-turn of about 80-90%.

q: 21. Good quality sand is never obtained from ............
explain: Sea sand contains salts (chlorides) that absorb moisture (deliquescence) and cause corrosion in reinforcement and efflorescence in masonry.

q: 22. For sanitary pipes and chemical stonewares,
explain: Salt glazing provides a highly resistant, acid-proof, and impermeable surface, making it ideal for pipes carrying sewage or chemicals.

q: 23. The usual percentages of clay and metal in cermet are
explain: Cermets (Ceramic-Metal composites) used in high-temperature applications often contain approximately 80% ceramic (clay/oxide) and 20% metal binder.

q: 24. The presence of sand in brick earth prevents
explain: Sand (Silica) forms the bulk of the brick and prevents shrinkage, cracking, and warping of raw bricks during the drying and burning process.

q: 25. The clay to be sued for manufacturing bricks for large project, is dugout and allowed to weather throughout
explain: Weathering is usually done by exposing the dug-out clay to the atmosphere throughout the monsoon to soften the mass and remove impurities.

q: 26. The harmonious mixing of the clay ingredients, is known as
explain: Blending is the process of mixing different clay ingredients or adding missing elements to the clay mass to achieve a uniform composition.

q: 27. The operation of removal of impurities or clay adhering to iron ores, is known as
explain: Dressing is the mechanical process of cleaning the ore to remove impurities (gangue) before it undergoes chemical treatment.

q: 28. If the iron ore contains clay as an impurity, the flux added during calcinations is
explain: Limestone ($CaCO_3$) is a basic flux added to react with acidic impurities like clay/silica to form slag that can be easily removed.

q: 29. First class timber has an average life of
explain: First-class timber (like Sal or Teak) is highly durable and can last more than 10 years even in exposed conditions.

q: 30. Refractory bricks are used for
explain: Refractory (fire) bricks are designed to withstand extreme heat without melting or cracking, making them ideal for lining furnaces and combustion chambers.

q: 31. The fire clay contains pure
explain: Fire clay is primarily composed of hydrated aluminum silicate (Kaolinite) with very low levels of fluxing agents like lime or iron oxide.

q: 32. Refractory bricks are
explain: Refractory bricks are categorized into acid (e.g., silica), basic (e.g., magnesite), and neutral (e.g., chromite) based on their chemical resistance to slag.

q: 33. Sewer pipes are made of ...............
explain: Stoneware is highly resistant to chemical attacks, corrosion, and erosion, making it the ideal material for conveying sewage which contains acids and gases.

q: 34. Advantage of clamp compared to kiln for burning bricks is that ...............
options: it takes less time for burning
it gives more output of first class bricks
it is suitable when bricks are required in large numbers
explain: Clamps are temporary structures and do not require the expensive permanent masonry construction needed for kilns, making them cheaper for small-scale operations.

q: 35. The internal size of mould used in brick preparation is ...............
options: equal to size of a fully burnt brick
smaller than the size of fully burnt brick
greater than the size of fully burnt brick
explain: Bricks shrink during the drying and burning processes. Therefore, the mould must be slightly larger (usually 8-10%) than the required finished size.

q: 36. Pug mill is used for ...............
explain: Pugging is the process of grinding and mixing clay with water to make it plastic and homogeneous, which is performed in a pug mill.

q: 37. Which of the following bricks are used for lining of furnaces?
explain: Refractory (fire) bricks are designed to withstand extremely high temperatures without melting or cracking, making them essential for furnace linings.

q: 38. The frog of a brick in a brick masonry is generally kept on ...............
explain: The frog (indentation) is kept upward so that it can be filled with mortar, creating a mechanical key between courses for better shear resistance.

q: 39. Glazing is used to make earthenware ...............
explain: Glazing applies a vitreous (glass-like) coating to the surface of ceramic ware, sealing the pores and making the item waterproof or impervious.

q: 40. Which of the following impurities is undesirable in the soil used for brick making?
explain: Kankar causes the brick to split, and alkalis cause efflorescence (white staining), making both undesirable for quality brick production.

q: 41. To improve the quality of bricks sometimes sand is added to the powdered soil. This process is known as ...............
explain: Blending is the process of adding specific materials (like sand or chalk) to the brick earth to correct its composition and improve its properties.

q: 42. The shape of the brick gets deformed due to rain water falling on hot brick. This defect is known as ...............
explain: Chuffs are the deformations or cracks caused by the rapid cooling of hot bricks when exposed to falling rain.

q: 43. The size of mould for bricks, is generally kept ...............
options: a little large to specified size
a little small to specified size
explain: Due to shrinkage during drying and burning, the mould must be slightly larger than the final required dimensions of the brick.

q: 44. The percentage of alumina in a good brick clay should vary from ...............
explain: Alumina provides plasticity to the clay. A content of 20-30% is ideal for moulding; excess alumina causes bricks to crack on drying.

q: 45. The type of glass used in glazing the north light trusses is ...............
explain: Wired glass contains a steel wire mesh for safety and fire resistance. It is commonly used in factory roofs and north light trusses to prevent glass from falling if shattered.

q: 46. In continuous flame type kiln, the maximum diameter of the kiln is at ...............
explain: The diameter is usually kept maximum at the mid-height to allow for a better distribution of heat and to facilitate the downward movement of the materials.

q: 47. Glazing of clay products, is done ...............
options: to protect them from atmospheric effect
to protect them from corrosive action
explain: Glazing serves multiple purposes: it makes the product impervious to liquids, protects it from weather, and provides a smooth, aesthetic finish.

q: 48. A pug mill is used for ...............
explain: Tempering is the process of bringing the clay to a proper degree of hardness and plasticity by mixing it with water, which is done in a pug mill.

q: 49. Bloating of bricks is due to ...............
options: presence of excess carbonaceous matter in the clay
presence of gas forming material in the clay
explain: Bloating is a spongy swell in bricks caused by gases trapped inside the clay during rapid heating when the surface has already fused.

q: 50. Swelling of bricks is known as ...............
explain: Bloating is the specific term used to describe the internal swelling of bricks due to trapped gases.
